raw:
These hypotheses rest on priors about NAS-Bench-201 (diminishing returns, redundancy of parallel paths, trainability from skip connections). I haven't run any of them against benchmark data.

Serial-path hypotheses (edges 0→1→2→3 and 0→2, 1→3):
1. Setting edge 5 to conv3x3 is worth less when edge 2 is already conv3x3, because the receptive field has already compounded and capacity is redundant.
2. Setting edge 5 to conv3x3 is worth more when edge 2 is avg_pool, because pooling followed by a conv gives complementary features.
3. Setting edge 4 to conv1x1 is worth more when edge 0 is conv3x3, because 1x1 channel mixing complements spatial features.
4. Setting edge 0 to conv3x3 is worth less when edge 3 is already conv3x3, because the direct path already supplies the capacity.

Parameter-free versus learnable parent:
5. Setting edge 3 to skip_connect is worth more when edge 5 is none, because the lost path leaves the skip as the main identity route.
6. Setting edge 1 to conv3x3 is worth less when edge 3 is skip_connect, because the identity path already supplies gradient flow and the extra conv is redundant.
7. Setting edge 4 to conv3x3 is worth more when edge 3 is avg_pool, because a pooled parallel branch lacks learnable capacity.
8. Setting edge 2 to avg_pool is worth less when edge 1 is conv3x3, because pooling adds little when a learnable parallel branch already feeds node 2.

Sum-sharing versus serial parents:
9. Setting edge 5 to conv3x3 is worth less when edge 3 is conv3x3, since parallel convs into node 3 are redundant.
10. Setting edge 4 to conv3x3 is worth less when edge 5 is conv3x3, since parallel convs into node 3 are redundant.
11. Setting edge 2 to conv3x3 is worth less when edge 1 is conv3x3, since parallel convs into node 2 are redundant.
12. Setting edge 1 to none costs less (higher accuracy) when edge 2 is conv3x3, because the cell keeps strong capacity via node 1.

Replace-op interactions:
13. Setting edge 3 to conv1x1 is worth less when it replaces conv3x3 than when it replaces something else, because that is a downgrade of the same edge.
14. Setting edge 0 to skip_connect is worth less (more harmful) when it replaces conv3x3, because it removes the main learnable path.
15. Setting edge 3 to none is worth more (less harmful) when edge 4 is conv3x3, because remaining parallel capacity compensates.

Connectivity-preserved removals and optimization:
16. Setting edge 4 to none costs less when edge 3 is skip_connect, because the identity path preserves trainability.
17. Setting edge 5 to avg_pool is worth more when edge 3 is conv3x3, because the pooled path adds a cheap regularising multi-scale branch next to a strong conv.
18. Setting edge 0 to conv3x3 is worth more when edge 2 is skip_connect, because the deep path then benefits without a trainability penalty.
19. Setting edge 5 to conv1x1 is worth more when edge 4 is none, because it becomes the main learnable route into the output.
20. Setting edge 2 to skip_connect is worth more when edge 5 is conv3x3, because the deep serial path is already learnable and an identity link improves gradient flow.
